audit.why: Zed owns the lane through his lethality spike, Vladimir only flips at full scaling; EVEN 5.5/10 with a 53.52% WR over 4497 games reflects that Vlad wins games, not lanes, here.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart carried blanket 'Skill' on rows 0-5 while content win[] and the packet levelChart agree on Zed x6 then Vladimir. Also every content whys[N] shipped with a debug-style 'win[N]=Zed: ' prefix visible to readers.

audit.corrected: Full sides flipped with why rewrites; prefixes stripped from whys.

audit.why: Ability names verified (Razor Shuriken, Living Shadow, Shadow Slash, Death Mark). Pool timing vs Death Mark correctly framed: the mark pops 3s after application and Pool's 2s untargetability eats the pop if spent after the mark lands, not on the opening dash. Energy costs (Q 75, W 40, E 40) now ground the trade windows.
Kit: R 120-100s, W 20-16s, Q 75 energy at rank 1, Vlad W 28s.

edits.before: - Zed Death Mark: matchup-defining — The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Sanguine Pool has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Death Mark: 120s at rank 1, 100s max — spend Pool AFTER the mark lands to eat the 3-second pop, never on the opening dash. - Living Shadow is 20-16s: with W down Zed has no escape and no double shuriken — that is your trade window. - Your 28s Pool has one job here.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, E-charge as he steps to answer, release and walk — the trade costs him HP and pays yours.
edits.after: His Q costs 75 energy at rank 1 — two whiffed volleys leave him energy-starved; Q the wave back and heal the chip.

edits.before: Pooling his poke and then eating the real engage at half HP with nothing — the pool is a combo-breaker, not a flinch reflex.
edits.after: Past river with your 28s Pool down, the W-R shadow engage has no answer left — you are the pick that starts their fight.
